app.title: The Needle & The Pin
app.tagline: Grow a trading city into a wealthy nation — and win only if that wealth also feeds, educates and protects its people.
app.credit: After Adam Smith's Wealth of Nations (1776) and al-Ghazali's Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din (c. 1100).

needle.name: The Needle (tutorial)
needle.desc: A single market town. Learn the four root crafts, the division of labour and the extent of the market. About 15 minutes.

britain1776.name: Britain, 1776
britain1776.desc: The flagship scenario. Mercantilist laws, the American war, early industry. Race the real history of British GDP and wages to 1850.

top.turnsCover: Treasury covers {n, plural, one {# turn} other {# turns}} of spending

farm.name: Farm
farm.desc: Grows grain on plains or fertile land (fertile +40%). Farming is a root craft.

pasture.name: Pasture
pasture.desc: Raises sheep for wool on plains or hills.

lumber.name: Lumber camp
lumber.desc: Cuts timber in forests: fuel for households and material for builders.

mine.name: Iron mine
mine.desc: Digs ore from hills or mountains with an ore deposit (grey dot).

bakery.name: Bakery
bakery.desc: Turns grain into bread, the first necessity.

weaver.name: Weaver
weaver.desc: Turns wool into cloth. Weaving is a root craft.

smithy.name: Smithy
smithy.desc: Turns ore into tools. Tools are what savings buy: they become capital.

builder.name: Builder's yard
builder.desc: Turns timber into housing. Building is a root craft.

pinworks.name: Pin workshop
pinworks.desc: Smith's pin factory. Little ore, many pins — if the market is wide enough.

port.name: Port
port.desc: On a coast. Ships reach foreign markets and import what you lack; sea lanes link your ports.

courthouse.name: Courthouse
courthouse.desc: Justice within 4 hexes: secure property, less fraud. Governance is a root craft.

granary.name: Public granary
granary.desc: Stores grain when it is cheap (funded by the relief budget) and releases it in dearth.

panel.nothing: Select a hex on the map, or pick a tool below to build.
panel.reachExplain: {r} buyers within reach. Each doubling allows one more level. Roads, rivers, ports and honest money widen it.
panel.explain: Output {out} = {workers} workers × {base} each × specialisation ×{spec} × tools ×{cap}{terrain, select, none {} other { × land ×{terrain}}}{fill, select, none {} other { × inputs {fill}}}
panel.bottleneck: Short of inputs: build more upstream.
panel.noBuyers: No buyers for much of the output.
panel.canGrow: Ready to split the work further next turn.
panel.needHands: Needs {n} workers to reach the next level.

cornLaw.name: Corn Law
cornLaw.desc: A heavy duty on foreign grain. Landlords cheer; bread costs more.

pinMonopoly.name: Pin monopoly charter
pinMonopoly.desc: Sell the pin trade to one company for a fee. Pins get dear and scarce.

breadPriceCap.name: Bread price cap
breadPriceCap.desc: Bread may not sell above its natural price. Queues and black markets when harvests fail.

guildRules.name: Guild apprenticeship rules
guildRules.desc: Seven years' apprenticeship. Masters are pleased; workers move between trades far more slowly.

internalTolls.name: Road tolls
internalTolls.desc: Revenue for the treasury and the lords — and every route costs more.

navigationActs.name: Navigation Acts
navigationActs.desc: Trade only in our own ships. Merchants protected; foreign markets retaliate.

testActs.name: Religious tests for office
testActs.desc: Only members of the established church may hold office.

debase.name: Debase the coin
debase.desc: Mix base metal into the coin: a large sum for the treasury now, then inflation and a collapse in Money Trust.

budget.title: The sovereign's budget
budget.intro: Smith's four duties of the sovereign, and Ghazali's granaries. Each line is a share of last turn's revenue.
budget.defenseDesc: Bandits and pirates raise every transport cost when defence is short.
budget.justiceDesc: Fair courts: secure property and less fraud.
budget.educationDesc: Literacy: faster labour mobility, Maslaha's intellect, institutions.
budget.reliefDesc: Fills the public granary and supports the poor.

tax.title: Tax design
tax.intro: Smith's four maxims, graded A to F. Bad design breeds smuggling, evasion and unrest.
tax.equalityDesc: Do people pay in proportion to their ability?
tax.certaintyDesc: Are amounts and timing clear, not left to a collector's whim?
tax.convenienceDesc: Is it collected when and how it is easiest to pay — without tempting smugglers?

inst.title: Institutions
inst.intro: Rules, money and trust make wealth possible. Develop one at a time; education and justice speed it up.

why.excluded: The other finance path was chosen

coinage.name: Coinage
coinage.desc: Coin of known weight. Removes the barter penalty on all trade.

lettersOfCredit.name: Letters of credit
lettersOfCredit.desc: Merchants settle at a distance; savings flow more easily.

banks.name: Interest banks
banks.desc: Fast credit growth and higher returns — and boom, bust and bank runs.

partnershipHouses.name: Partnership houses
partnershipHouses.desc: Mudaraba and musharaka: profit and loss shared. Slower, steadier, kinder to Maslaha.

centralBank.name: Central bank
centralBank.desc: A lender of last resort: Money Trust recovers faster and higher.

depositInsurance.name: Deposit insurance
depositInsurance.desc: No more runs on sound banks.

marketSquares.name: Market squares
marketSquares.desc: Town populations count 20% more toward market reach.

merchantShipping.name: Merchant shipping
merchantShipping.desc: Cheaper sea lanes and double port capacity.

canals.name: Canals
canals.desc: Unlocks canals: the cheapest inland transport before rail.

hisba.name: Hisba office
hisba.desc: The market inspector: fraud falls fast and grain hoarders can be broken.

contractCourts.name: Contract courts
contractCourts.desc: Enforceable contracts: less fraud, prosecution of cheats.

jointStock.name: Joint-stock companies
jointStock.desc: Pooled capital: every building and work costs 25% less.

factoryActs.name: Factory Acts
factoryActs.desc: Limits on child labour: households and children protected; output −4%.

elementarySchools.name: Elementary schools
elementarySchools.desc: Raises the literacy the nation can reach.

printingPress.name: Printing press
printingPress.desc: Literacy grows half as fast again; public schooling develops faster.

learnedSocieties.name: Learned societies
learnedSocieties.desc: Inventions spread half as fast again.

publicSchooling.name: Public schooling
publicSchooling.desc: Schooling for every child: literacy rises much faster and higher.

class.laborersWant: Want cheap bread, jobs and schooling. Ignored: riots, emigration, revolution.
class.merchantsWant: Want low taxes, monopolies and protection. Ignored: capital flight.
class.landlordsWant: Want grain tariffs and a low land tax. Ignored: they block reforms.

scotsman.widen: Widen the market and the rest follows. Your best shops are waiting on roads, not on hands.
scotsman.tariffs: Every duty you lay on foreign goods is a duty on your own people, and your neighbours will answer in kind.
scotsman.guilds: Seven years to learn a trade a clever lad could learn in weeks. The guild rules keep hands where they are not wanted.
scotsman.coin: A coin that cheats its holder will not be held for long. Mend the money before anything else.
scotsman.monopoly: A monopolist keeps the market understocked. You granted it; you can revoke it.
scotsman.schools: For a small expense the public can teach nearly every child to read, write and count.
scotsman.tolls: Tolls on every road shrink every market. Take the gates down.
scotsman.fine: The country prospers. Keep the coin true, the roads open and the courts honest.
scotsman.debt: The debt grows. Interest paid today is investment lost tomorrow.
scotsman.capitalShort: Savings are what equip the workshops. Do nothing to frighten them away.

scholar.bread: There are families who cannot buy bread. Wealth is a means; ask what it is for.
scholar.fraud: Short weights and hidden defects are spreading. The market that cannot trust itself will shrink.
scholar.mirror: The coin is a mirror for the value of all things. You have clouded it.
scholar.richFor: The merchants grow rich while the poor leave on every ship. Rich and brittle is not the goal.
scholar.poor: The poor are restless and the stores are empty. Fill the granary in good years.
scholar.knowledge: Knowledge is a protection the state owes, as much as bread and safety.
scholar.worship: No one should be shut out of office for how they worship. Trust needs open doors.
scholar.fine: Bread is honest and the coin is true. Guard what you have built.
scholar.hoard: Coin is being buried, not spent. Money that is hoarded fails at its work.
scholar.crafts: A people needs four crafts before a market: farming, weaving, building, and someone to keep order.

event.title: A matter for the council
event.chooseFirst: Answer the council before the year can end.

reckoning.title: The Reckoning of {year}
reckoning.intro: A chapter closes. History is read against your nation.
reckoning.whatIfIntro: Pick one decision from the last chapter. The same years are replayed with it reversed — same seed, same weather, same luck.
reckoning.reform: Choose one reform to define the next chapter

openPorts.name: Open the ports
openPorts.desc: Customs down to 8%, the Navigation Acts repealed, foreign markets 30% wider. Protected merchants and landlords grumble.

repealCornLaws.name: Repeal the Corn Laws
repealCornLaws.desc: Foreign grain enters freely, for good. Landlords are furious; bread gets cheaper.

canalMania.name: Canal mania
canalMania.desc: Establish canals at once (costs 30% of a year's revenue).

foundCentralBank.name: Found a central bank
foundCentralBank.desc: A lender of last resort, established at once.

publicSchoolingAct.name: Public schooling act
publicSchoolingAct.desc: Schooling for every child; education budget at least 12%.

factoryReform.name: Factory reform
factoryReform.desc: Factory Acts at once. Masters object; families gain.

debtConsolidation.name: Consolidate the debt
debtConsolidation.desc: Lower interest on the national debt; trust +4.

poorLawReform.name: Reform the poor law
poorLawReform.desc: Relief of at least 8% of revenue, administered fairly.

marketInspectors.name: Market inspectors
marketInspectors.desc: The hisba office established at once.

repealTestActs.name: Repeal religious tests
repealTestActs.desc: Office open to citizens of every confession, for good.

ending.title: {year}: the verdict

golden.name: Golden Age
golden.desc: Rich and good: both meters above target, and history beaten.

gilded.name: Gilded Age
gilded.desc: Rich, but brittle: Opulence above target, Maslaha below.

pious.name: Pious Stagnation
pious.desc: Fair, but stagnant: Maslaha above target, Opulence below.

collapse.name: Collapse
collapse.desc: The nation fell before its time.

reason.revolution: Revolution: the laborers rose after years of despair.
reason.bankruptcy: State bankruptcy: interest swallowed the revenue.
reason.famine: Famine: too many died for want of bread.

ending.medal: Medal: you beat the ghost of history by 25% or more.

tutorial.market: In year {year} all four root crafts stood, and a market formed.

war.lost: The colonies were lost all the same, and the war debt remained.

resign.scotsman: In {year} the Scotsman resigned from the council.
resign.scholar: In {year} the Scholar of Tus resigned from the council.

meter.opulenceIntro: Rebuilt each turn from five measures. The real wage of the lowest laborer weighs most: Smith's own test of a nation's wealth.
meter.maslahaIntro: Ghazali's five protections, each 20%. Faith is measured as freedom of worship and trust in honest institutions — never which religion a nation follows.
meter.interaction: High Opulence with low Maslaha brings bubbles, unrest and emigration. Both above 60 earns the Good Society bonus: institutions develop faster and crises strike less often.

part.realWage: Real wage of the lowest laborer

partDesc.realWage: Wage ÷ cost of a basic basket of bread, cloth, fuel and rent (welfare ratio).
partDesc.gdppc: Real output per head, in the scenario's units.
partDesc.capital: Tools and machines per worker, against the start.
partDesc.reach: Share of people living inside well-connected markets.
partDesc.trade: Imports and exports per person, against the start.
partDesc.nafs: Necessities secured, and how comfortably the poorest can afford them; famine deaths count against it.
partDesc.nasl: Household stability: wages, work, housing, relief and child welfare.
partDesc.mal: Money Trust, honest markets and fair courts.
partDesc.din: Trust in institutions, honest markets, and freedom of worship.

ghost.title: Ghost of history
ghost.noData: No historical series for this scenario.

tutorial.title: The Needle
tutorial.goal: Goal: Opulence {o} and Maslaha {m} by year 20.
tutorial.step0: Your town already farms. Build a Weaver, a Builder's yard and a Courthouse near it (Workshops and Civic tools below).
tutorial.step1: A market has formed. Build a Pin workshop next to the town and select it: see the gold catchment of its market.
tutorial.step2: Your pin workshop is stuck at level 1: its market is too small. Lay a road to the next village and watch the catchment grow.
tutorial.step3: Develop Coinage (Institutions). Barter halves every market; honest coin removes the penalty.
tutorial.step4: Balance both meters: fund schools and justice, keep bread cheap, and keep the coin true.

help.title: How to play
body: You don't command citizens. You set the conditions — roads, money, laws, institutions — and the invisible hand does the rest: workers move to better-paying shops on their own, and merchants found new workshops where prices are high.

Every workshop has a specialisation level from 1 to 5. Each level splits the work among more specialists and multiplies output per worker. But a workshop can only specialise as far as its market reach allows: select a workshop to see its gold catchment.
Prices rise when goods are scarce and fall in a glut. A price spike is a signal: it pulls workers and capital in.
Each turn: read the market, build, play up to two policy cards, set taxes and budget, develop an institution, then End turn. Events ask the council for a decision.
You win by raising both meters above the scenario's targets: Opulence (Smith) and Maslaha (Ghazali). In Britain, 1776, the ghost of history races you.
Keys: E end turn · B budget · T taxes · I institutions · C codex · O cycle overlays · 1–9 tools · Esc close · WASD/arrows pan · +/− zoom.
